Sarah — great to see the momentum. Attached is a first-pass cost workbook (MAP_cost_model_v1.xlsx) and a one-page summary in the workbook. Quick summary below so you can paste into your MAP doc:

- Baseline tokens/$: $0.0018 per 1k tokens for r-generation path (model quantized, q4), measured on a mixed prompt profile (long + short).
- Prompt mix assumption: 55% short (<64 tokens), 30% medium (64-512 tokens), 15% long (>512 tokens).
- Caching: prefix/KV cache expected hit rate 28% in week-1 (conservative), improving to 45% steady-state with aggressive prefixing. Cache benefit reduces token generation by ~20-30% on average; we modeled 22% in the spreadsheet.
- Batching: we used a 40ms batching window for throughput path; effective tokens-per-second calculations assume an average batch size ~3.6 for peak traffic. If you want lower p99 latency we can shrink window to 20ms which reduces batching efficiency by ~18% (cost up).
- Prefetch / warm-up: we included a one-time prefetch amortized cost for 10% of requests that require an embedding lookup; this adds ~0.6% to overall token spend in the model.

Known risks called out in workbook: prompt churn (hard to predict), cache warming time, and traffic skew (bursty sessions cause lower batching efficiency).

Proposed MAP milestones (short):
1) 6/3–6/6: Validate assumptions using your production traffic sample (we'll run a 1k request sim with your distribution).
2) 6/9: Ops canary run (10–25% traffic; conservative default 20%).
3) 6/12: Decision point — procurement/legal sign & move to full pilot (if canary metrics meet SLOs).

Next steps: please share the traffic sample (anonymized) and we'll run the sim. Ben and Monica (cc'd) will own the sim and procurement alignment respectively.

Attachment: MAP_cost_model_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Looping in technical detail for the sim so expectations are clear. TL;DR: we need a distribution + header length histogram; we'll run 1k requests, 3 runs (cold, warm, steady). Notes: 

- Batching window: the 40ms window in Karthik's sheet assumes continuous steady-state traffic at the target QPS. For more bursty real-world traffic, batching falls back to smaller sizes — in sim we'll include an "arrival jitter" profile so you can see sensitivity.
- Cache hit rate: our conservative 28% is based on other healthcare pilot traffic we've seen with moderate templating. If your prompts include patient-specific tokens (IDs, notes) hit rate will be lower; templating your prompts (prefix constants) will increase hit rate quickly.
- Short prompt overhead: for requests <32 tokens, per-request overhead (scheduling, RPC) dominates; batching helps but improvements plateau. We will surface tokens-per-dollar for three slices: short, medium, long.
- Prefetch: if you plan to precompute embeddings for known doc sets, we model that as a background job; prefetch amortization is separate from real-time inference spend.

Deliverable from the sim: per-slice tokens-per-dollar, p50/p95 latency, and observed cache hit rate over the 3 runs. I'll attach the sim log after the first run.

Attachment: prefetch-sim-run.log

- SOW & Billing: legal will need a short SOW itemizing expected usage bands and billing cadence. If HelixMed can accept monthly billing with a committed baseline, we can include a credit mechanism for overage protection.
- Invoicing lead time: procurement typically needs 5 business days from signed SOW to issue PO; add that into calendar if you need a PO before 6/12.
- Canary size: recommended conservative default is 15% for the first week to validate both cost and observability (we can go to 25% if the sim shows strong cache/batching benefits).
